The cloister is the coolest place in the building by two o'clock.
They walked the cloister twice and settled the whole argument.
A colonnade of fourteen columns, two of them modern copies.
The colonnade gives shade on the side that needs it.
The cornice was replaced in fibreglass and nobody has noticed.
Water ran behind the cornice for years before the ceiling fell.
Desalination solved the supply and doubled the energy bill.
Three desalination plants and still a queue at the standpipe.
Swallows nest under the eaves every April.
Snow slides off the eaves in one piece and usually onto the path.
The effluent was within the limit and the limit was written in 1972.
Effluent from the dye works coloured the stream for a decade.
The road climbs the escarpment in eleven turns.
Villages sit along the foot of the escarpment where the springs are.
The fen was drained in the 1930s and the soil is still sinking.
Birds that left the fen have come back since the pumps were turned off.
The date is cut into the stone gable: 1897.
A gable end that has been rebuilt twice in living memory.
Mother-of-pearl inlay in a door that has been outside for a century.
The inlay is original; the frame around it is not.
Eleven coats of lacquer, each one polished before the next.
The lacquer has crazed but the colour underneath is untouched.
The lintel is a single piece of stone two metres long.
Crack the lintel and the whole wall above it has to come down.
The mausoleum was restored in 1988 and again in 2014.
A mausoleum of blue tile that the photographs never get right.
The minaret leans by about a metre and has done for four hundred years.
From the top of the minaret you can see where the old canal ran.
A line of pylons crosses the valley where the road cannot.
The pylons were repainted grey and are no less visible.
Refining happens near the port and the crude comes by pipeline.
Two stages of refining and the metal is still not pure enough.
Smelting began here in the 1930s and closed in 2004.
The smelting works employed nine thousand people at its peak.
The substation failed and four districts went dark at once.
A new substation was built behind the depot in 2011.

Roads and borders have made transhumance harder every decade.
A vicarious pleasure in a journey he will never make.
Vicarious liability means the employer answers for the employee.

grammar.label: editing another person's prose
grammar.form: the minimal intervention; the query rather than the change; preserving voice
grammar.meaning: improves a text without replacing its author

explanation.en: The discipline of editing is restraint: change what is wrong, query what is unclear, and leave what is merely different from how you would have written it. An editor who imposes a voice has produced their own text with someone else's name on it, and every writer can tell.
explanation.uz: Tahrirning mohiyati — o'zini tiyish: xatoni tuzat, noaniqni so'ra, o'zingcha boshqacha yozgan bo'larding degan narsaga tegma.

grammar.positive_example: I have queried three sentences and changed two. The rest is hers.
grammar.negative_example: I have rewritten the piece in a cleaner style throughout.

l1_notes.uz: Tahrirdagi o'zini tiyish — professional me'yor; boshqa an'analarda tahrirchi erkinroq bo'lishi mumkin.

grammar.label: knowing when a text is finished
grammar.form: the last pass for cuts only; the test of reading aloud; the point of diminishing returns
grammar.meaning: stops revising before the text is polished into blandness

explanation.en: Every text reaches a point where further revision removes what made it worth reading. The signs are recognisable: you are moving commas, you are reinstating yesterday's cuts, the sentences are all the same length. The last useful pass is for cuts alone, and after that the text is finished whether or not it is perfect.
explanation.uz: Har bir matn shunday nuqtaga yetadiki, keyingi tahrir uni o'qishga arzirli qilgan narsani yo'q qiladi. Belgilari aniq: vergul ko'chirmoqdasan, kechagi qisqartmalarni qaytarmoqdasan.

grammar.positive_example: I made three cuts on the last pass and then stopped, which is the rule I keep.
grammar.negative_example: I revised it eleven more times until every sentence was the same length.

l1_notes.uz: Tugatish vaqtini bilish tajriba bilan keladi; belgilarini oldindan bilish uni tezlashtiradi.

body.text: I have Dilnoza's article and I have marked forty things on it.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: How many of the forty are errors?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Places where I would have written it differently.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then you have six marks to make. The rest is hers.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Some of them really are better my way.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Better in your voice. She is twenty-four and she is building one. Take it off her now and she will write like a committee for ten years.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: When do I stop editing my own?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: When the changes stop making it better and begin only making it different. You will feel the day it happens.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I rewrote the first paragraph nine times last week.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then the piece was finished on Tuesday and you spent four days finding that out. It is normal, and it is still four days.
